thesis: Permian Basin Royalty Trust is a passive Texas express trust created in 1980 that owns net profits interests in Permian Basin oil and gas properties. **[Fact]** Argent Trust Company is trustee; there are no employees and no operating business. **[Fact]** Unitholders receive monthly cash distributions from two property groups: a **75%** net profits interest on Waddell Ranch (Crane County, operated by Blackbeard Operating) and a **95%** net profits interest on legacy Texas Royalty properties (Riverhill Energy). **[Fact]** **46,608,796** units were outstanding at March 27, 2026 (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260327_rpt20251231_acc0001193125_26_128561.htm`). **[Fact]** The trust is grantor-trust taxed; unitholders receive K-1s. Proved reserves at December 31, 2025 totaled **19.7 million** barrels of oil equivalent on properties underlying the royalties.
why_market_wrong: The unit price may embed Permian oil optionality and a corporate-conversion narrative while the filing floor is a depleting distribution stream with Waddell Ranch in excess cost. **[Inference]** Horizon Kinetics holds **12.5%** of units (Schedule 13G in 10-K); SoftVest (**13.3%**) won court approval in May 2026 to ease indenture amendments, raising conversion speculation. **[Inference]** At **~$29** the market pays roughly **2.5×** the SEC standardized-measure reserve value (**~$12** per unit at year-end 2025), so yield-focused buyers may overpay if Waddell stays cost-burdened. **[Inference]** K-1 complexity and depletion keep the name off dividend screens, but that cuts both ways: it can also hide overpricing versus engineer-discounted cash flows.
